timing: Complete release Wasm processes with input, output and exit; no MoonX and no startup subtraction
slowdown_policy: The shared-foundation integration accepts the measured small abstraction costs. A ratio above this review boundary is never offset against another workload's gain.
coverage_policy: Compare all82 releaseWasm artifacts. Changed artifacts require actual genuine-input timing rows; correctness-only dispositions cannot qualify a performance change. Every applicable required real mode and local boundary witness must complete. No synthetic or command-specific timing runner.

separate_required_evidence.sort-spill-8m: The pre-foundation baseline exceeded 20 seconds in warmup at -S 1M. Retain that failure. Validate the candidate with the same deadline and compare its bytes with the baseline default-budget sort; this is a repair observation, not an old/new speed ratio.
separate_required_evidence.resources: Observe kernel peak RSS, temporary residue and cleanup separately from timing. Single-pair resource observations are not stability qualification.
separate_required_evidence.correctness: Run the applicable Wasm unit and functional suites, including errors, partial output, cancellation, early exit, Unicode and binary cases. Timing fixture coverage alone is insufficient.

strategies.invariant: Encoding retains at most four unfinished input bytes and a wrap column between bounded reads. Complete quanta can be emitted before EOF; padding and the final newline occur only on successful EOF. Failed writes are not replayed. Decoding retains its existing whole-input read-error contract.
strategies.measurement_scope: Complete genuine-source wrapped/unwrapped and pipe encoding rows; synthetic RSS and open-producer diagnostics remain separate.

strategies.invariant: A 64 KiB input read leaves at most two carry bytes. Complete quanta reach the writer before another read; only final carry receives padding. Wrap columns persist across chunks, and failed output never replays or finalizes carry.
strategies.measurement_scope: Local genuine-source encoding and binary controls; unchanged decoder behavior, no general throughput, RSS or publication claim.
